author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Elizabeth Elkin
description: The Trump administration is preparing to expand the opportunity for sales of higher-ethanol E15 gasoline this summer by waiving the fuel from US volatility requirements, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Trump Officials Ready E15 Waiver for Summer Gasoline Sales

description: Michael Claesson, Supreme Commander and Chief of Defense of the Swedish Armed Forces, discusses NATO's potential involvement in the Middle East conflict, risks to European security, links between Iran and Russia, and the implications for defense spending and military capacity. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Swedish Defense Chief Michael Claesson on NATO Role, Iran Risks and Security

description: Barbara Leaf, former US Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern Affairs under President Biden and Distinguished Diplomatic Fellow at the Middle East Institute, discusses prospects for US-Iran negotiations, leadership dynamics in Tehran, risks around the Strait of Hormuz, and the role of military force alongside diplomacy. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Former Diplomat Warns Military Alone Won't Solve Crisis

author: Martha Viotti Beck
description: Brazil is preparing a new program to provide financing to companies struggling with the impact of US tariffs and the war in the Middle East.
title: Lula Readies $3 Billion Plan for Companies Hit by Tariffs, War

description: Rep. Jake Auchincloss, Democratic Congressman from Massachusetts and member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, says US gains in air dominance have been offset by Iran's sea denial advantage, warns of a looming "quagmire," and says he will not vote for additional funding requests from the Pentagon. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Auchincloss Slams War With Iran as 'Strategic Failure'

author: Paul-Alain Hunt
description: Rio Tinto Group has secured a A$2 billion ($1.4 billion) government bailout to keep the Boyne aluminum smelter in Australia running until at least 2040 and support its transition to renewable electricity.
title: Rio Tinto Secures Bailout for Aluminum Smelter in Australia

description: Could the US be heading for military action in Cuba? Big Take host Sarah Holder talks to Bloomberg’s Eric Martin and Jim Wyss about what Trump has said about “taking” the island. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Trump "Taking" Cuba Could Mean

author: Sanne Wass, Sara Sjolin
description: Danish parliamentary elections remain too close to call, complicating Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen’s bid for a third term in office.
title: Danish Ruling Party’s Bloc in Narrow Lead to Win Election

description: President Donald Trump says Iran gave the US a "very big present worth a tremendous amount of money." Trump wouldn't say what it was, but did confirm it was related to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. He spoke at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Gave the US a 'Present,' Trump Says

description: At a Space Force base in the mountains of Colorado, the US and Canada are still tight. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Andreas Kluth went there for an inside look. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: This US-Canada Military Base Is Still Strong

author: Nancy Cook
description: Cornyn and Paxton are left to fight it out until a runoff in May.
title: Trump Decides to Sidestep Texas GOP Fight Over Senate Nomination

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss broader market reaction amid more back and forth about US-Iran talks. Ray Takeyh from the Council on Foreign Relations and former US Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross join the show to discuss. Then, Bloomberg Tech Co-Hosts Ed Ludlow and Caroline Hyde sit down with Applied Intuition CTO and co-founder Peter Ludwig to discuss the company's tech partnerships in the defense space. Then, Bloomberg Leveraged Finance reporters Ellen DiMauro and Olivia Fishlow join to discuss more private credit stress at Cliffwater. Also, live remarks from President Trump as he delivers live remarks from the White House, saying Iran has offered a "present" as a show of good faith in negotiations. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks Bounce From Lows on Hopes for US-Iran Talks | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/24/2026

description: Jim Kessler, executive vice president for policy at the center left think tank Third Way, said that new data shows that on the whole Democratic primary voters are more moderate than how they are portrayed in the media.  Kessler said that Democrats are primarily concerned about electability heading into the 2026 midterms and the 2028 presidential elections, and want a candidate that is a 'fighter' for reform.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Democrat Voters Looking For a 'Fighter,' Says Third Way Survey

description: “We’re in negotiations (with Iran) right now,” President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House, noting that special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as well as Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vice President JD Vance are all involved. Trump says Iran's Navy and Air Force are all gone.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Wants to Make a Deal, Trump Says

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, former US Ambassador Daniel Fried, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Bluestack Strategies Founder Maura Gillespie and Crusoe CEO Chase Lochmiller. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Pushes on Iran Peace Talks | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/24/2026

description:
President Trump took questions from reporter on the war in Iran and a potential deal to fund the Department of Homeland Security after he swore-in Markwayne Mullin as the new head of DHS. 
Trump doubled down on his assertion that the US has already 'won' the war with Iran and told reporters that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vice President JD Vance are taking part in negotiations. 
President Trump was also asked about a potential deal to fund DHS. Trump told reporters he thought lawmakers were getting close on a deal, but indicated he likely wouldn't be happy with legislation if it didn't include voter ID provisions.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Negotiations Ongoing, As Trump Says 'War Has Been Won' (Q&A)

author: Joe Lovinger, Josh Wingrove, Catherine Lucey
description: The Republican Party is weighing Dallas as the host location for its midterm convention as President Donald Trump looks to drum up voter enthusiasm ahead of elections determining which party controls Congress for the final two years of his term.
title: Republican Party Eyes Dallas for Unusual Midterm Convention

description: "They're totally defeated," President Donald Trump says when asked whether he was hopeful a peace deal would be successful in ending the war in Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran War 'Has Been Won'

description: Bloomberg's Lydia Beyoud has been reporting on the growing prevalence and legal battles surrounding prediction markets. She joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto."  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lawmakers Target Sports Bets on Prediction Markets

description: Former US Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross discusses the long-term impact of the Iran war on geopolitics and global markets. He speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War Shows US Isn't a 'Sleeping Dragon,' Wilbur Ross Says

author: Sanne Wass
description: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen’s party is on track to win the most seats in a parliamentary election shaped by Donald Trump’s threats over Greenland, according to exit polls.
title: Danish Premier Takes Lead in Election Shaped by Trump

author: Elizabeth Elkin
description: The Trump administration is “moving at warp speed” to get out biofuels blending standards, with an announcement coming “sooner rather than later,” according to US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins.
title: US Moving at ‘Warp Speed’ to Finish Biofuels Rules, Rollins Says

description: George Bush Intercontinental Airport in Houston warned passengers that wait times could top four hours after officials shut down some TSA checkpoints and halted all PreCheck and CLEAR operations. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: TSA Lines Anger Flyers in Houston

author: Daniel Carvalho, Augusta Saraiva
description: A Brazilian Supreme Court judge ruled that Jair Bolsonaro can temporarily serve his sentence for plotting a coup under house arrest, allowing the former president to leave prison due to his deteriorating health.
title: Judge Grants Bolsonaro Temporary House Arrest Amid Health Woes

author: Vinicius Andrade, Jorgelina Do Rosario, Nicolle Yapur, Irene Garcia Perez
description: Dozens of hedge-fund and oil-company executives are gathering this week in Caracas, where Venezuela’s acting president, Delcy Rodriguez, signaled an interest in re-opening the nation’s economy to foreign businesses, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Hedge Funds, Oil Companies Meet in Venezuela to Chart a New Era

author: Jen Judson
description: The US is planning to deploy about 3,000 troops from the 82nd Airborne Division to the Middle East, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday, as the White House weighs options to ease Iran’s choke-hold on the Strait of Hormuz.
title: US to Deploy 82nd Airborne Troops to Middle East, WSJ Says

description: NASA administrator Jared Isaacman says he’s confident that the agency will have the cash it needs to build a new moon base President Donald Trump has asked for. He says some resources have to be moved around. He speaks on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: NASA Has the Means to Get to the Moon, Isaacman Says

author: Maggie Eastland, Carmen Arroyo
description: Top Trump administration advisers urged Congress to enact a national standard for artificial intelligence oversight that follows the legislative framework sent to US lawmakers aimed at preempting a growing number of state rules.
title: Trump’s AI Advisers Urge Congress to Pass National Set of Rules

author: Donato Paolo Mancini, Alessandra Migliaccio
description: Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni called on Tourism Minister Daniela Santanche to resign as she attempts to clean house after a defeat in a key referendum this week, in a sign of growing turmoil within her government.
title: Meloni Demands Minister Exit in Growing Post-Referendum Turmoil

author: Erik Wasson, Steven T. Dennis, Alicia Diaz
description: Senate Democrats have rejected the latest offer from President Donald Trump and Republicans to fund most of the Department of Homeland Security and end a lengthy shutdown that has snarled airport security checkpoints and threatened to ripple through an economy already roiled by the Iran war.
title: DHS Shutdown Persists as Democrats Reject Trump-Backed Offer

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Courtney Subramanian
description: Iran and Israel showed no signs of letup in the 25th day of the war, further unsettling global markets even as US President Donald Trump’s administration signaled momentum toward arranging formal talks to end the conflict.
title: Iran, Israel Trade Strikes Amid US Claims of Peace Talks

description: United Airlines Holdings Inc. Chief Executive Officer Scott Kirby says security lines at airports have gotten longer in the last week, but he thinks the partial government shutdown is coming to an end and TSA agents need to get paid. He speaks to Lisa Abramowicz. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: United CEO Says TSA Agents Need to Get Paid Now

description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged his Iranian counterpart to engage in negotiations as soon as possible with the US to end the war in the Middle East, according to a government statement on Tuesday.
title: China’s Wang Yi Pushes Iran to Talk With US About Ending War

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier arrived at a port in Crete on Monday after it had to leave the Middle East — and the war against Iran — when a fire broke out in its laundry area. But the massive ship’s problems run a lot deeper than that.
title: US Aircraft Carrier That Left Mideast Over Fire Has Other Issues

description: Iran’s biggest Gulf Arab neighbors are considering joining the US-Israeli war against Iran, and could be pushed to if Tehran attacks their critical infrastructure, according to several people with knowledge of the situation.
title: Gulf States Weigh Military Options to Counter Iran’s Escalation

description: Finland put on ice a plan to move its election platform to Amazon Web Services Inc., the latest development in Europe’s drive towards digital autonomy as trust in the US frays.
title: Finland Shelves Plan to Move Election Platform to Amazon Servers

author: Marissa Newman
description: Iranian missiles have fallen near Jerusalem’s holiest sites, raising the risk of igniting a broader religious conflict across the Middle East. Whether by accident or design, Iran has repeatedly sent projectiles hurtling in the direction of the Al-Aqsa Mosque, the Western Wall and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, which are sacred to Muslims, Jews and Christians, respectively.
title: Why Iran’s Jerusalem Strikes Risk Sparking a Broader Religious Conflict

author: Julian Lee
description: Value of shipments hits most since just after Ukraine invasion, amid higher prices and flows
title: Russia Boosts Its Oil Revenues to Four-Year High as Prices Surge

description: President Donald Trump claimed JPMorgan Chase & Co. Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon “personally directed” the closure of his accounts, meriting Florida state jurisdiction over his $5 billion “debanking” suit.
title: Trump Argues to Keep JPMorgan ‘Debanking’ Lawsuit in Florida

description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said the war in Iran “is emboldening” Russia as his country’s capital came under renewed barrage of air strikes.
title: Zelenskiy Says Iran War Emboldens Putin as Russia Renews Strikes

description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he discussed the Iran war on a call with President Donald Trump, including the conflict’s impact on the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for India’s energy imports.

description: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves said the UK government is contingency planning for “every eventuality” over the economic impact of the Iran crisis, and reaffirmed that any potential help for Britons would be targeted at the neediest.
title: UK’s Reeves Planning for ‘Every Eventuality’ on Iran War Impact

description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu asked close confidant Ron Dermer to monitor US-Iranian negotiations aimed at ending the war and make sure the country’s interests are upheld, an Israeli official said.

description: Ireland’s government approved a €250 million ($290 million) package to alleviate the impact of soaring energy costs caused by the Iran war, including a cut to the fuel excise duty.

description: The economy, inflation and immigration are the top issues for Latinos ahead of the US midterms.

description: La economía, la inflación y la inmigración son las principales preocupaciones de los latinos en EE.UU. de cara a las elecciones de mitad de mandato.

description:
Latino voters, who helped seal President Donald Trump’s return to power in 2024, could be the reason why he loses control of the House and, possibly, the Senate. 
 (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Russia is delaying a decision aimed at reducing its dependence on energy income as oil prices surge on the back of the war in the Middle East.

description: New head of DHS must reform ICE’s tarnished image

description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent regularly says his motivation to get “out from behind my desk” and enter public service was concern about growing US debt. Developments over the past several weeks have left those alarms ringing even louder.

description:
On today's show, Iran's deputy parliamentary speaker denies any negotiations with the US are taking place, calling President Trump's claim "psychological warfare". It comes after Trump told reporters the US would delay strikes against Iran's energy infrastructure after what he called "productive conversations" with the country. Meanwhile, the Wall Street Journal reporting that Gulf states are inching toward joining the fight against Iran.

A stocks rally eased, while Brent crude rebounded and gold extended its slump on renewed caution over the Middle East.

The European Union and Australia have agreed to a free-trade deal after almost a decade of talks. The two sides looking to boost ties in the wake of rising tariffs from the United States.

Today's guests: Hetal Mehta, Chief Economist at St James's PlaceTrashline:
Corrects spelling of the name of our EMEA Grains reporter at 00;38;15 in video (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Refutes Trump Talks Claim & Gulf Weighs Joining War: WSJ | Daybreak Europe 3/24/2026

description: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko will make his first visit to North Korea, as the two sanctioned states look to build ties.
title: Belarusian President Lukashenko to Make Visit to North Korea

description: Cape Town Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis appears set to win an internal election as head of South Africa’s second-biggest political party next month, with a little-known municipal councilor his only challenger for the post.
title: Cape Town Mayor Is Favorite to Lead South Africa’s No. 2 Party

description: The US and Israel continued to bombard Iran overnight, while Kuwait and Bahrain reported retaliatory strikes by Iranian missiles. Countries including Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Oman have engaged in back-channel talks with Iran to contain the war and seek a ceasefire. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Kuwait, Bahrain Hit by Iran Strikes as Optimism Fades

author: Patrick Sykes, Fiona MacDonald
description: Fighting between Iran and the US-Israeli alliance continued unabated, even as President Donald Trump claimed talks are under way to end the conflict.

description: Following are the edited highlights of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s interview on Tuesday at the presidential palace in Manila with Bloomberg Television’s Haslinda Amin.
title: Read the Edited Highlights of Marcos’s Interview With Bloomberg

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon
description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is open to restarting talks with Beijing on a joint oil and gas project in a disputed area of the South China Sea, saying the war in Iran may provide the impetus for a breakthrough.
title: Marcos Says War May Spur Energy Talks With China in Disputed Sea

description: The European Union and Australia agreed to a free-trade deal, announced Tuesday in Canberra by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. The two sides also signed a Security and Defence Partnership. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: EU, Australia Agree to Trade Deal, Defense Partnership
US Stock Futures Down, Oil Up on Iran War Escalation Fears

description: Donald Trump’s decision to back down from his threat to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure is happening amidst reports of potential talks facilitated by regional powers. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace breaks down what we know so far. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why Did Trump Back Down From Iran Power Threat?

author: Faseeh Mangi, Tooba Khan
description: Pakistan is making a push to mediate talks to end the US-Israeli war against Iran, with its powerful army chief holding calls with President Donald Trump to find a resolution to the fighting, people familiar with the matter said.
title: Pakistan Seeks to Mediate Peace Talks With US, Iran in Islamabad

author: Yongchang Chin, Dan Murtaugh
description: Contracts representing millions of barrels of oil changed hands about 15 minutes before a social media post from US President Donald Trump that sent crude prices tumbling by as much as 14%.
title: Oil Market Saw Trading Spike Before Trump’s Iran Pivot Post

description: Danes are casting their ballots on Tuesday in a general election that’s shaping up to be a vote for stability after US President Donald Trump’s threats over Greenland.
title: Denmark Votes as Trump’s Greenland Claims Loom Over Election

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: Senators in both parties expressed rising optimism late Monday about reaching an agreement to end the five-week partial shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security, which has increasingly snarled air travel across the United States.
title: Senate Optimistic on Deal to Fund DHS as Airport Chaos Balloons

description: President Donald Trump says the US will postpone strikes against Iran’s energy infrastructure after what he called “productive conversations” with Tehran. But his comments spurred confusion over the participants in the talks and parameters of a deal. Bloomberg's Laura Davison reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Delays Energy Strikes, Sets Five Days for Iran Talks

author: Kevin Crowley, Serene Cheong, Ari Natter
description: Houston’s showpiece energy conference is usually an opportunity for backslapping and glad-handing. But this year executives are nervously watching the impact of the Iran war and the lack of any clear path toward a resolution.
title: Energy Bosses Share Iran Anxieties at Key Houston Gathering

author: Carolina Gonzalez, Matthew Malinowski
description: Chile’s fuel prices will soar this week after the government announced on Monday night that it will loosen a stabilization mechanism to reflect the international oil shock, Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz said.
title: Chile Hikes Fuel Prices By Up to 54% to Reflect Global Oil Shock

author: Yoshiaki Nohara, Akemi Terukina
description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi ordered a close review of the entire supply chain for oil-related products as the country scrambles to cope with the fallout from the war in Iran.
title: Takaichi Orders Review of Entire Supply Chain for Oil Products

author: Philip Glamann
description: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have taken steps toward joining the Iran war, the Wall Street Journal reported, potentially signaling an escalation of the fighting.
title: Saudis and UAE Take Steps Toward Joining Iran War, WSJ Reports

author: Soo-Hyang Choi
description: South Korea’s Prime Minister Kim Min-seok called off his planned visit to China this week, citing an urgent need to remain at home to manage the widening economic and livelihood impacts of the Iran war.

description: The conflict in Iran is pushing Middle Eastern countries toward South Korea’s lower-cost air defense systems, opening a new opportunity to expand its arms export footprint beyond Europe.

author: Alicia Diaz, Caitlin Reilly
description: Markwayne Mullin was confirmed Department of Homeland Security secretary, placing the Oklahoma senator in charge of a Trump administration immigration crackdown that has triggered a 37-day funding shutdown of the cabinet agency.
title: Mullin Confirmed to Lead DHS, Head Trump’s Immigration Crackdown

author: James Mayger, Jorge Valero
description: The European Union and Australia agreed to a free-trade deal, wrapping up almost a decade of talks as the two sides push to tighten ties and reinvigorate a rules-based order that’s under assault from the Trump administration.
title: Europe, Australia Agree to Trade Deal to Boost Ties, Defy US
